messages:
alex: Heads up — after the routing weight change rolled yesterday I'm seeing a ~40ms bump in p95 for a subset of endpoints (mostly /v1/generate). p50 looks unchanged. Anyone else see this?
lin: saw the same on our dashboard. p95 spike localized to route B variants. link: https://console.redwood/latency?slice=routeB (internal) :eyes:
jordan: That was the sticky-weight rollout i merged yesterday morning. deploybot: deploy jordan/route-weighting v2 -> prod finished at 2145675200 :white_check_mark:
maria: p50 stable + p95 increase = tail issue, could be change in sampling or rollup attribution. Do we aggregate by endpoint or by route?
sam: Our rollup is per-endpoint, but we attach a sampling key that's sometimes normalized away during merge. If route-level weights aren't preserved in telemetry, heavier traffic to a slower shard could skew p95 at endpoint-level.
alex: Sam — can you paste the query you're using to compute rollups? I want to reproduce locally.
sam: sure. quick example SQL we use for telemetry rollups:
```
SELECT endpoint, tdigest_merge(tdigests) AS td, tdigest_percentile(td, 0.95) AS p95
FROM telemetry_agg
WHERE time >= now() - interval '1h'
GROUP BY endpoint;
```
The problem: telemetry_agg's labels set sometimes drop the route tag when samples are merged across collectors.
maria: ohhhh that explains why only some endpoints show it — the route tag was the only dimension separating fast vs slow variants. Without it the heavy slow variant dominates the rollup.
lin: for immediate triage: can we surface a per-route breakdown in the p95 chart (toggle)? even a temporary split would prove whether the weight change is the cause.
jordan: agree — UX-wise the console should default to endpoint+route breakdown when a rollout/weighting is active. Right now it flattens too aggressively which hides regressions.
ci-bot: incident created: INCIDENT-2026-214567 - p95 uptick on /v1/generate (assigned to alex)
alex: I'll add route_id back into the rollup keys and run a trimmed re-aggregation for the last 6h. If that shows variance, we should revert the weight tweak or adjust routing policy.
sam: long-term we should change the sampling_key to include route_weight_id so merges keep that dimension. Also add an override in the exporter: `preserve_tags = ["route_id", "route_weight_id"]`.
maria: small UX ask for the console: add a 'show-sampling' overlay that marks when sampling or merge normalization happened on a given time window. Could be a tiny badge on the chart.
alex: timeline: i'll push a hotfix to telemetry keys in the next 30m, trigger re-agg, and post results. If rollout is root cause we can throttle route B back.
jordan: :thumbsup: thanks. can someone add a short note in the rollout page explaining that percentiles can change when weights change? new users keep getting surprised.
lin: filed RD-4523 to add per-route p95 toggle + sampling overlay in console (assign: maria).
maria: i'll pick up RD-4523 after the dashboard freeze. For now i'll add an ephemeral annotation to the /v1/generate chart pointing to INCIDENT-2026-214567.
alex: quick repro command if anyone wants to run locally: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://telemetry.internal/api/query?agg=tdigest&group=endpoint,route_id&from=-6h" | jq .`
sam: after the re-agg i suspect p95 on routeB will explain the 40ms delta. if so, we should add a test in rolled canary checks to compare endpoint-level vs route-level p95 drift when weights change.
jordan: good call. add a gating rule: if endpoint p95 moves >5% and route-level p95 explains >80% of drift, block auto-rollout.
alex: noted. i'll update the rollout controller PR with that gating condition.
ci-bot: re-aggregation job queued: job_id=ragg-2145679001
lin: thanks team. keep updates here and if alex posts numbers i'll circulate to oncall. :eyes:
